summary.headline: India Pesticides FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR 1,078 crore and PAT 45.8% to INR 120 crore; Q4 domestic sales up over 50% to INR 183 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 crossed INR 1,000 crore revenue for the first time, with EBITDA up 44.7% to INR 194 crore at an 18% margin. Q4 growth was driven by domestic herbicides and intermediates (domestic INR 183 crore vs INR 118 crore), while Q4 exports fell to INR 84 crore from INR 89 crore on geopolitical disruption and pricing pressure. Management said raw material and freight inflation is being partly passed to customers, with sulphur-based inputs seeing the largest increases. Management reiterated the INR 3,000 crore revenue target for March 2031 and guided FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% with EBITDA margin of 18-20%. Dividend was held at INR 0.75, which drew pushback from an individual investor.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 118 crore in Q4 FY25 (>50%)
vs INR 89 crore in Q4 FY25 (decline)

segments.name: Technicals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 744 crore. Pretilachlor and PEDA intermediates drove volume growth after backward integration; the combined plant capacity is about 8,500 MT, running at an expected 70-75% utilisation with a 3-month seasonal shutdown around Aug-Oct.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 311 crore. Capacity scaled to 10,000 MT, with distribution across 18 states through 24 depots and over 340 sales personnel.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports INR 408 crore (about 39% of revenue) across more than 35 countries. Q4 exports were INR 84 crore, down from INR 89 crore on geopolitical issues in March 2026.

segments.name: Shalvis (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: First technical product started with about INR 4-5 crore revenue in FY26. Management expects at least INR 25 crore in FY27 from this molecule and guides total Shalvis revenue of INR 70-80 crore in FY27 including a second block expected by Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin projected at 18-20%; management said 18% holds for the year.
INR 3,000 crore revenue target reiterated for March 2031, with Shalvis contributing about INR 1,000 crore and existing plants (Dewa Road, Sandila, formulations) about INR 2,000 crore.
Net working capital days could improve by a further 10-12 days by FY27, though inventory levels are rising as customers now buy on spot basis.
FY27 capex: INR 45 crore for India Pesticides and INR 90 crore for the subsidiary, mainly funded by internal accruals; a small loan may be taken at the subsidiary.
PEDA and Pretilachlor FY27 volumes expected to be better than FY26 with full utilisation of the capacity commissioned in March 2026.
risks_watch: Raw material and freight inflation tied to Middle East tensions and sulphur-based inputs; ability to keep passing costs to customers.
Export softness from geopolitical disruption and pricing pressure in certain exported products (Q4 exports down YoY).
Below-normal monsoon forecast (IMD 6-8% deficit) and El Nino uncertainty for agro demand.
Competition and margin pressure as new domestic producers enter Pretilachlor/PEDA.
Execution of the Shalvis second block by Sep-Oct 2026 and the Hamirpur new molecules, both key to the INR 3,000 crore by FY31 target.
Management did not state a cause for the paraquat substitution question; no product confirmed as a substitute.
Working capital pressure from higher inventory and dividend payout versus the 5-15% policy; credit rating review in September 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, capacity and the INR 3,000 crore FY31 target, but cautious on exports, pricing visibility and supply chain. Several answers were vague on quantification (price increases, incremental revenue, Hamirpur timing), and the dividend response was defensive.
key_quotes: A key milestone during the year was India Pesticides Limited crossing the INR 1,000 crores revenue mark for the first time, reflecting the company's strong execution capabilities and expanding market presence.
We have done some long-term arrangements with some of our suppliers who are able to bring the material to us in time.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how much price increase had been taken across the portfolio and whether demand is holding up because of inventory running out or China price hikes.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China is also raising prices and the company has passed on some cost differential, with customers accepting increases for some products; an average across the portfolio was not given because sulphur-based products rose more and need more discussion with customers.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Shalvis and Pretilachlor/PEDA contribution in FY26 and expectations for FY27, including the second Shalvis block.
qa_highlights.answer: Shalvis contributed about INR 4-5 crore in FY26 (CFO repeated INR 4 crore); FY27 at least INR 25 crore from the first molecule and total Shalvis revenue INR 70-80 crore including the second block expected by September-October 2026. PEDA and Pretilachlor volumes expected to be better than FY26 with full use of capacity commissioned in March; no incremental revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 EBITDA margin guidance and working capital trajectory.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided EBITDA margin of 18-20%; net working capital days at 223 could improve by about 10-12 days by FY27, though inventory must rise as customers now buy on spot basis rather than quarterly planning.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR 68 crore capital work in progress and the INR 27 crore subsidiary term loan, plus cost of funds.
qa_highlights.answer: Of the INR 68 crore CWIP, INR 18 crore is at India Pesticides and most is at Shalvis, to be capitalised once the second Shalvis plant is operational; the term loan of about INR 27 crore at the subsidiary costs about 8%, and working capital borrowing is about 7.2-7.3% (50 bps over FDR). Credit rating is A+ and due for review in September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the INR 3,000 crore FY31 target is intact and how it breaks down between Shalvis and existing plants.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the INR 3,000 crore target for March 2031; Shalvis expected to contribute about INR 1,000 crore and existing Dewa Road, Sandila and formulation plants about INR 2,000 crore. Management also said IMD forecasts 6-8% below-normal rainfall but production has held in past deficit years.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the dividend of INR 0.75 relative to profit and whether a higher payout or buyback is possible.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the dividend policy is 5-15% of net profit and the company chose to keep the existing payout to fund subsidiary capex and working capital from internal accruals; CEO said small dividend increases would not materially change investor returns and the focus is on revenue and profit growth.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex budget: INR 45 crore for India Pesticides standalone and INR 90 crore for the 100% subsidiary Shalvis, mainly funded through internal accruals; a small loan may be taken at the subsidiary.

Combined Pretilachlor and PEDA capacity about 8,500 MT, expected utilisation 70-75% given a roughly three-month seasonal shutdown around August-October; FY27 volumes expected to be better than FY26 with full use of capacity commissioned in March 2026.
Formulations capacity scaled to 10,000 MT; distribution across 18 states through 24 depots and over 340 sales personnel.

Shalvis: first technical product started with about INR 4-5 crore revenue in FY26; at least INR 25 crore expected in FY27 from that molecule plus two more molecules this year; second block expected operational by September-October 2026; total Shalvis revenue guided at INR 70-80 crore in FY27.

Hamirpur facility: development work progressing with infrastructure and operational blocks; two entirely new molecules targeted this year, primarily for export; management expects about 10% share of a herbicide market it says is large, though no timeline or market size in rupees was given.

Sandila site is full with no space for expansion; FY27 plan is one intermediate and one technical-grade product there plus balancing equipment to augment capacity, hence lower capex. Q4 capital work in progress was INR 68 crore, of which INR 18 crore at India Pesticides and the balance mainly at Shalvis; part to capitalise in Q4 FY27 and the rest in FY27-28.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 domestic sales rose more than 50% YoY to INR 183 crore (from INR 118 crore), driven by herbicides and intermediates; management cited about 30% volume growth in the quarter.

Q4 exports were INR 84 crore vs INR 89 crore; management said exports were about 5% lower QoQ and attributed the dip to geopolitical issues in March 2026 and pricing pressure in certain products. FY26 exports INR 408 crore (about 39% of revenue) across more than 35 countries.

Price increases taken to pass on raw material and freight costs; management could not give an average increase across the portfolio, said sulphur-based inputs rose more, and said some customers agreed to pass-through while prices are expected to hold in coming months.

Pretilachlor and PEDA: management said domestic production now fully replaces imports after antidumping duty; new capacity expected to cover Indian requirement, leaving room for one or two new producers; margins on these products are slightly below company average but expected to hold.
Japanese partner forecast for FY27 and FY28 about 30% higher than last year; one more molecule sample submitted and awaiting feedback.
Management said China is also raising prices, the company is seeing supply-chain strain from Middle East tensions, and demand is described as okay with limited price variation for these molecules.

adds.what: Shalvis second block (subsidiary) supporting INR 70-80 crore FY27 Shalvis revenue
Sandila intermediate and technical-grade products plus balancing equipment to augment capacity (site full)
Hamirpur facility: two new export-oriented molecules under development, no timeline or rupee size given

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (held) with EBITDA margin 18-20%, backed by full use of capacity commissioned March 2026, Shalvis guidance of INR 70-80 crore (second block by Sep-Oct 2026), a Japanese partner forecast ~30% higher, and price pass-through; no firm order book quantified, and Q4 exports fell 5% QoQ.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was guided at 18-20% against 18% in FY26 (up from 15.9% in FY25), but the margin range is essentially flat-to-up, with raw material and freight inflation only partly passed through and sulphur-based inputs rising most.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (Shalvis second block by Sep-Oct 2026); Sandila augm
rows.why: Shalvis second block firmly guided for Sep-Oct 2026 with INR 90 crore FY27 subsidiary capex, and Sandila (site full) plans one intermediate and one technical-grade product with INR 45 crore capex from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 domestic sales rose over 50% to INR 183 crore with about 30% volume growth, full use of March 2026 capacity is planned, and FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% on a INR 1,078 crore base; exports softness (INR 84 crore in Q4) is the offset.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 72.5% (70-75% guided with a 3-month Aug-Oct shutdown), so a new capex announcement is not forced; the FY27 INR 45 crore + INR 90 crore budget is already set, and a Hamirpur timeline or size was not given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 volumes for Pretilachlor/PEDA will beat FY26 with full use of capacity commissioned in March 2026, and Japanese partner forecast is ~30% higher for FY27 and FY28, but no quantified upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 exports fell to INR 84 crore from INR 89 crore (down ~5% QoQ) on geopolitical and pricing pressure, sulphur-based input inflation is rising, and IMD forecasts 6-8% below-normal monsoon, though FY27 guidance of 15-20% growth and 18-20% margin was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY27 (second Shalvis block by Sep-Oct 2026; two more Shalvis
rows.why: Shalvis expects at least INR 25 crore from the first molecule plus two more molecules in FY27 and total Shalvis revenue of INR 70-80 crore, which is a concrete plan from a 4-5 crore base in FY26; Hamirpur's two export molecules have no timeline.

rows.label: Japanese partner FY27/FY28 forecast ~30% higher; one more molecule sample awaiti
rows.why: Partner forecast is about 30% above last year for FY27 and FY28, but it is a forecast rather than a firm order and one sample is still awaiting feedback.

rows.label: Net working capital days down 10-12 by FY27 from 223 days
rows.why: NWC days fell from 254 to 223 in FY26, and management guided a further 10-12 day cut, but inventory is rising as customers move to spot buying, which works against it.

rows.label: Credit rating review September 2026; subsidiary term loan ~INR 27 crore at ~8%
rows.why: Rating is A+ and due for review in September 2026, and a small subsidiary loan may be taken to fund the INR 90 crore Shalvis capex, which is mainly funded from internal accruals.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15-20% FY27 growth, 18-20% margin, INR 3,000 crore FY31 target and Shalvis ramp, but vague on portfolio price increases, Hamirpur timing and incremental revenue; analysts pushed on pricing, capex funding and the defensive dividend answer.
